entries.name: Max Glass v. RWA Company LLC

arguments_rejected_or_waived: King v. VeriFone exception: rejected. Plaintiff misreads King, which the Supreme Court said is not an endorsement of the practice. Even under Plaintiff's broad reading, the plenary claims have not been dismissed with leave to amend, and Plaintiff has already filed his amended plenary complaint.

Khanna exception (overlap caused by defendant's incomplete production): rejected. In Khanna the inspection action came first and the plenary filing followed under limitations pressure, whereas here the sequence was reversed (fn. 63). Plaintiff identified no specific timing pressures, and the fact that he would not have needed to demand had RWA produced does not equal Khanna-type pressure.

Valuation purpose is independent and the parallel-action case law reaches only the investigation purpose: rejected as unconvincing. The Court did not separately analyze valuation and found no special circumstances supporting either purpose.
Request that the Court defer the investigation purpose rather than dismiss (raised at oral argument): rejected. The Court recommended dismissal with prejudice.
RWA accepted valuation as a purpose by producing records and only later called the purpose pretextual: rejected among the arguments the Court found unconvincing, without separate analysis.

RWA failed to prove pretext, and overlap in requested documents does not prove pretext: rejected. The dispositive point was that the duplicative plenary filing defeats proper purpose absent special circumstances.

authorities_cited.proposition: LLC member inspection right invoked by the demands and the Complaint.

authorities_cited.authority: CHC Invs., LLC v. FirstSun Cap. Bancorp, 2019 WL 328414 (Del. Ch. Jan. 24, 2019)
authorities_cited.proposition: Absent special circumstances, parallel plenary and inspection actions defeat proper purpose. The Khanna ruling is limited to timing pressures caused by the defendant, or at least not caused by the plaintiff. A plaintiff must state a proper purpose.

authorities_cited.authority: Schnatter v. Papa John's Int'l, Inc., 2019 WL 194634 (Del. Ch. Jan. 15, 2019), abrogated on other grounds by Tiger v. Boast Apparel, Inc., 214 A.3d 933 (Del. 2019)
authorities_cited.proposition: Filing a plenary mismanagement action undercuts the claimed need for inspection to investigate the same mismanagement.

authorities_cited.authority: Bizzari v. Suburban Waste Servs., Inc., 2016 WL 4540292 (Del. Ch. Aug. 30, 2016)
authorities_cited.proposition: A plenary filing on the same issues effectively concedes the records are not necessary or essential to an investigation purpose.

authorities_cited.authority: Highland Select Equity Fund, L.P. v. Motient Corp., 906 A.2d 156 (Del. Ch. 2006), aff'd, 922 A.2d 415 (Del. 2007)
authorities_cited.proposition: Using inspection to investigate pending plenary claims undermines discovery law.

authorities_cited.authority: Baca v. Insight Enters., Inc., 2010 WL 2219715 (Del. Ch. June 3, 2010)
authorities_cited.proposition: No proper purpose exists in investigating matters the stockholder already put at issue in a plenary action. Also cited for taking judicial notice of parallel-proceeding filings.

authorities_cited.authority: Engels v. D2 Pharma Consulting LLC, 2025 WL 3903893 (Del. Ch. Dec. 31, 2025)
authorities_cited.proposition: Court declined to enforce a § 18-305 demand given a pending plenary proceeding where records were obtainable in that forum.

authorities_cited.authority: Central Laborers Pension Fund v. News Corp., 2011 WL 6224538 (Del. Ch. Nov. 30, 2011)
authorities_cited.proposition: VeriFone does not authorize using inspection tools while actively pursuing a simultaneously filed plenary action at its early stages.
A § 18-305 demand functions analytically like a Section 220 demand.

authorities_cited.authority: An v. Archblock, Inc., 2025 WL 1024661 (Del. Ch. Nov. 7, 2023) (as cited)
authorities_cited.proposition: The Khanna exception does not apply where the limitations period is not close to expiring.

authorities_cited.authority: KT4 P'rs LLC v. Palantir Tech., Inc., 203 A.3d 738 (Del. 2019)
authorities_cited.proposition: The plaintiff must prove each category is essential to the stated purpose, and inspection is not comprehensive discovery.

authorities_cited.authority: King v. VeriFone Hldgs., Inc., 12 A.3d 1140 (Del. 2011)
authorities_cited.proposition: Inspection to aid repleading was permitted where the plenary complaint had been dismissed without prejudice with leave to amend. Here the plenary claims were not dismissed and an amended complaint was already filed.

authorities_cited.authority: Khanna v. Covad Commc'ns Grp., Inc., 2004 WL 187274 (Del. Ch. Jan. 23, 2004)
authorities_cited.proposition: Inspection rights were not waived where the inspection action preceded the derivative suit and the defendant's noncompliance created limitations pressure.

authorities_cited.authority: Romero v. Career Educ. Corp., 2005 WL 3112001 (Del. Ch. Nov. 4, 2005)
authorities_cited.proposition: A later derivative filing does not necessarily extinguish all proper purposes.

authorities_cited.authority: Sanders v. Ohmite Holdings, LLC, 17 A.3d 1186 (Del. Ch. 2011)
authorities_cited.proposition: Section 18-305 is construed by reference to analogous corporate and partnership statutes.

authorities_cited.authority: Cent. Mortg. Co. v. Morgan Stanley Mortg. Cap. Hldgs. LLC, 27 A.3d 531 (Del. 2011)
Ferris v. Ferris Props., Inc., 2020 WL 6606062 (Del. Ch. Nov. 12, 2020)
authorities_cited.proposition: Inspection orders must be tailored with rifled precision.
Basis of the motion to dismiss.
Final report in a summary proceeding, with exceptions due within three days.

summary.brief_summary: RWA Company, LLC moved under Rule 12(b)(6) to dismiss member Max Glass's § 18-305 action seeking records for valuation and mismanagement purposes. Glass had filed a plenary action against RWA and its principals two days before his first demand, and he sued here after the Plenary Defendants moved toward a discovery stay. The Magistrate held that the overlapping plenary action refutes proper purpose, because Delaware enforces parallel inspections only in special circumstances. Neither the King v. VeriFone exception nor the Khanna exception fit, since the plenary claims were never dismissed with leave to amend, the plenary suit came first, and no defendant-caused timing pressure was identified.
summary.core_legal_issue: Whether an LLC member stated a claim to compel inspection under 6 Del. C. § 18-305 for the stated purposes of valuing his membership interest and investigating mismanagement, where he had filed an overlapping plenary action against RWA and its fiduciaries two days before his first demand, had served discovery in that action, and sued here only after the Plenary Defendants moved toward a discovery stay. Put differently, whether any 'special circumstances' exception (King v. VeriFone or Khanna) permits parallel inspection.

flags.evidence: I recommend that the Motion to Dismiss be granted and the Complaint be dismissed with prejudice. This is a final report pursuant to Court of Chancery Rule 144(d)(2)
flags.opinion_says: The recommendation, final-report status and three-day exceptions period are stated. The opinion says nothing about fees, and the same-documents-through-discovery point is only the Company's argument.
flags.problem: The opinion never addresses attorney's fees or costs, so the statement that no fees were awarded is not in the text.

summary.holding: The Magistrate recommended that RWA's Motion to Dismiss be granted and the Complaint dismissed with prejudice. Plaintiff's duplicative, earlier-filed Plenary Action, which covers the same matters and in which he had already sought the same documents through discovery, defeats proper purpose absent special circumstances. Neither the King v. VeriFone exception (plenary claims not dismissed; amended complaint already filed) nor the Khanna exception (reverse sequence; no identified timing pressure) applies. Plaintiff cannot use § 18-305 to circumvent Plenary Action discovery but may pursue discovery there, if and when appropriate, subject to Chancellor McCormick's ruling on the pending motion to dismiss. This is a final report under Ct. Ch. R. 144(d)(2), and exceptions may be filed within three business days. No fees awarded.
key_facts_and_concessions: Plaintiff filed the Plenary Action on October 20, 2025, naming RWA among the Plenary Defendants, two days before his October 22, 2025 written § 18-305 demand. The Court took judicial notice of the Plenary Action filings.

Plaintiff served fourteen interrogatories, twelve requests for production and eight requests for admission in the Plenary Action on May 5, 2026, and refused on May 28, 2026 to agree to a discovery stay. He filed this action on June 8, 2026. His counsel filed a letter of non-opposition to the Plenary Defendants' Motion to Stay Discovery on June 29, 2026.

The plenary claims have not been dismissed. Plaintiff filed an Amended Verified Complaint on August 12, 2026 asserting twenty-one counts, and briefing on motions to dismiss it is underway. The Motion to Stay Discovery is pending and no stay has been entered (fn. 24).

RWA's argument, accepted by the Court, was that the books and records sought relate directly and expressly to allegations, claims and relief sought in the Plenary Action and should be pursued through discovery there.

Plaintiff's stated purposes in all demands were valuation of his membership interest and investigation of potential mismanagement. The June 2, 2026 Supplemental Demand sought fourteen categories and expressly superseded the June 1 version (fn. 15).

After a Confidentiality Agreement, RWA produced the current Operating Agreement and 2022-2024 financial statements on November 5, 2025 and additional financials on November 6, 2025. Correspondence confirmed that no board minutes, resolutions or written consents exist for May 23, 2022 to the present. On November 7, 2025, RWA advised that the financials previously provided were incorrect (fn. 10).

RWA refused the November 19, 2025 revised demand as unrelated to the stated purpose and 'an impermissible fishing expedition.' Through counsel, on June 3, 2026, it refused any inspection, calling the demand an end-run around Plenary Action discovery.
summary.practical_takeaway: A member or stockholder who sues first and demands later, particularly one who has already served plenary discovery seeking the same documents, should expect a § 18-305 or § 220 action to be dismissed with prejudice unless King-type leave-to-amend or Khanna-type defendant-caused timing pressure can be shown. Pairing a valuation purpose with an investigation purpose did not save the demand here, and the Court did not separately analyze valuation.
summary.standard_of_review: Ct. Ch. R. 12(b)(6) reasonable conceivability: well-pleaded allegations accepted as true and reasonable inferences drawn for plaintiff. Substantively, the plaintiff must state a proper purpose and show each category is essential to that purpose (Section 220 standards applied to § 18-305).
